author: harness:claude-code

patch.value:
## The basis, from the implementation

`src/sdk/graph/governance.ts` documents every reachability field as "a typed hierarchy or implements path to an outcome". The admitted set is therefore `parent`, `child`, `implements` — three of the ten built-in kinds.

## What that excludes, counted on the live graph

The audit's own `edges_by_kind` for this tracker:

| kind | edges | admitted by reachability |
|---|---|---|
| related | 5,570 | no (correctly: undirected, no semantics) |
| implements | 2,592 | yes |
| parent | 2,276 | yes |
| blocked_by | 589 | no |
| discovered_from | 494 | no |
| verifies | 254 | no |
| blocks | 243 | no |
| supersedes | 84 | no |
| child | 8 | yes |
| incident_from | 4 | no |

`semantic_edges` is reported as 836 — `discovered_from` + `verifies` + `supersedes` + `incident_from`. Every one of those 836 edges contributes zero to the reachability numbers that `graph-outcome-reachable-floor` (2434), `graph-outcome-unreachable-ceiling` (15) and `graph-outcome-reachability-basis-points-floor` (9938) enforce at block severity.

## The population it mislabels

Recomputed independently: traversing `--kind parent,child,implements` inward from the six outcome milestones plus pm-doxj reaches 2,443 of 2,455 items. The twelve it does not reach are pm-doxj itself, which is the index root rather than an outcome, and eleven canceled items:

- eight archived PRD-era epics: pm-6hhn, pm-zetb, pm-murz, pm-met4, pm-xtfo, pm-gyfn, pm-defw, pm-lty
- three accidental probe items: pm-11ag, pm-crpv, pm-lql3

The eight archived epics are the sharp case. They are not unlinked. pm-9rgaal — itself an outcome milestone — records `supersedes` pointing at pm-6hhn, which is precisely the correct statement of what happened to it. The item was retired the right way and the invariant still scores it as unreachable.

Traversing with `--kind` unrestricted reaches all 2,455. So the items are connected; only the basis refuses the connection.

## The ontology asymmetry underneath

Of the ten built-in kinds in `src/sdk/relationship-kinds/contract.ts`, four declare an `inverse`: `blocked_by`/`blocks` and `parent`/`child`. `related` is undirected and needs none. Five directed kinds declare no inverse at all: `discovered_from`, `incident_from`, `implements`, `verifies`, `supersedes`.

For `implements` this is harmless, because the edge is stored on the item that does the implementing and therefore already points toward the outcome. For `supersedes` it is the opposite: the edge is stored on the living item and points at the dead one. The archived item has only an incoming edge, so there is no spelling it can store to say what replaced it, and no outward path from it to anything living.

That is why widening the basis and giving `supersedes` a reverse spelling are two halves of one repair, and why doing only the first would leave the direction wrong.

## Duplicate check

Searched all statuses for reachability, traversal, ontology and inverse-spelling items. pm-bzmeaa owns the reachability invariant itself and its acceptance criteria are about depth distribution, hop policy and waivers — not about which kinds count. pm-3dyec2 owns the four traversal verbs rejecting semantic kinds on the query surface, which is a different surface from the governance computation. pm-h6b73t owns the ladder being a sibling set rather than a layer. pm-q6n8sj, now closed, bounded `related` and introduced semantic share. No item covers the reachability basis admitting only three kinds.

value.text:
Decisive evidence for the basis claim, measured 2026-08-13 by recomputing reachability from the six outcome milestones plus pm-doxj over the on-disk edge set, parsing both TOON dependency encodings.

Over the full edge basis every one of the 2,467 items reaches an apex: zero unreachable. Over the basis the governance code actually admits — parent, child, implements — exactly 11 do not: the eight canceled PRD-era epics pm-6hhn, pm-zetb, pm-murz, pm-met4, pm-xtfo, pm-gyfn, pm-defw and the archived duplicate pm-lty, plus the three canceled probe items pm-11ag, pm-crpv, pm-lql3.

The part that settles the argument: every one of those eleven already carries a correct, evidence-backed, recorded edge to a reachable node, and in every case it is a supersedes edge stored on the living side. pm-2xl supersedes pm-6hhn, pm-u9r supersedes pm-zetb, pm-c0r supersedes pm-murz, pm-54d supersedes pm-met4, pm-f45 supersedes pm-xtfo, pm-b1w supersedes pm-gyfn, pm-jiw supersedes pm-defw, pm-j7a supersedes pm-lty. The historical spine pm-1w6scp describes as missing is in fact present and correct in the data.

So the unreachable population is not a data gap and there is nothing to backfill. It is entirely an artifact of excluding one edge kind from the basis, and it is the specific kind whose semantics — this replaced that — is what a timeline query needs most. Recording that edge is the right modelling act and it moves the metric by zero, which is the strongest possible statement of this item's thesis: a project cannot improve a number the basis refuses to read.

Corollary for the remedy. Widening the basis to include supersedes takes audit-basis unreachable from 11 to 0 without adding a single edge. That is worth doing before any further reachability ratchet, because a floor tightened against the narrow basis would permanently price in the exclusion.
